operations.comment: ; Read routine contracts at their entries. CPU RAM, OAM shadow, PPU and PRG are distinct spaces.
; The 16-byte iNES header describes mapper 3, fixed 32 KiB PRG and four 8 KiB CHR banks; preserve it verbatim.
; The hardware vector words at $FFFA-$FFFF point to these three jump stubs at $8000-$8008. NMI dispatches to the frame service below.
; Reset enters the cold initialization path.
; IRQ is unused by this program and returns immediately.
; Disable rendering and interrupts, wait for PPU startup, then clear all 2 KiB of CPU RAM. Initialize stack, APU, CHR bank, sprites and random seed before entering the campaign controller.
; Wait for two pairs of vblank observations before touching PPU state. The inner BIT loops poll hardware rather than the software frame counter.
; Clear the same offset in each CPU RAM page; Y wrapping finishes all eight pages.
; No IRQ service is installed.

; Preserve A/X/Y; DMA the shadow OAM, drain queued VRAM transfers, apply pending attributes and palette animation, restore scroll/control, tick audio and sample controllers. Increment the frame counter last.
; Latch both standard controllers and shift eight serial bits into packed button bytes. Compare the previous high and low nibbles separately to produce change flags, not per-button rising edges.
; Busy delay using X outer counts and a wrapping Y inner count. Rendering synchronization is not implied; A is preserved, X/Y are consumed.
; Wait X frame boundaries using the shared vblank helper. X must be nonzero.
; Clear the PPUCTRL NMI bit in hardware and its shadow while preserving A.
; Set the PPUCTRL NMI bit in hardware and its shadow while preserving A.
; When NMI is disabled poll PPUSTATUS vblank; otherwise wait for the NMI frame counter to change. The helper does not drain a queue itself.
; Wait until an interrupt changes the frame counter; callers must have enabled NMI.
; Wait a frame and clear the background visibility bits in the mask shadow.
; Wait a frame and enable background visibility, including the left edge.
; Wait a frame and clear sprite visibility bits in the mask shadow.
; Wait a frame and enable sprite visibility, including the left edge.
; Clear both visibility groups and wait five frames so the NMI applies the mask.
; Enable both visibility groups, align the software frame phase, then wait for the change to be applied.
; Hide sprites/background, disable NMI and allow a CPU delay before direct PPU access.
; Enable NMI, allow two frames, then reveal background and sprites.
; Build a 16-color dim palette from the low color nibbles of sourcePtr. Enqueue it, enable display, then raise brightness by $10 toward each source color over eight delayed passes.
; Keep colors already at their target; raise the others one brightness band and send the staged palette through the VRAM queue.
; Over eight passes subtract a brightness band or replace dark colors with $0F. Queue each 16-color palette, delay, then blank and disable NMI.
; Clear the PPU address-increment bit and record queue stride 1.
; Set the PPU address-increment bit and record queue stride 2, meaning a vertical step of 32 PPU bytes.
; Restore control and both scroll writes from their shadows, then read status to reset the PPU address latch. Preserve A.
; Set every OAM Y coordinate to $F8; tile, attribute and X bytes are left intact.
; A supplies nametable high bits, X column and Y row. Add the coordinate lookup pair and write PPUADDR; rows >=31 also leave the resulting address in ppuAddressLo/Hi.
; Same row/column lookup as SetPpuCoordinates, but return the address in ppuAddressLo/Hi for a queued transfer. Preserve the row in Y.
; Select PPU address $2000 and restore scroll/latch state, preserving A.
; A selects nametable high byte, X is fill tile. Write 30 rows of 32 tiles, excluding attributes.
; Copy four 256-byte pages from sourcePtr to the selected PPU page. Advance the source high byte after each page.
; A selects nametable high byte; add 3 and use low byte $C0. Fill the 64-byte attribute table with X.
; Copy 64 attribute bytes from sourcePtr to the selected nametable's $3C0 offset.
; Read 64 attributes into attributeShadow after discarding the PPU read-buffer byte. Save the destination address for later NMI updates.
; Initialize the two-byte random state to $110E.
; Advance an eight-step shift/XOR generator using feedback $B4. Preserve Y; return the new high state byte in A.

; Decode a compact stream directly to PPUDATA. The first five bytes are dictionary values; zero ends the stream. Commands use low five bits as count: $E0 repeats the next byte, $C0 increments from it, $A0 copies literals, other high groups repeat a dictionary byte. Source pointers advance between commands.
; Choose repeat, incrementing, literal or dictionary mode from the command's high three bits.
; Copy 16 bytes from each of sourcePtr and secondaryPtr into adjacent background/sprite palette shadows, then upload all 32 colors.
; Wait for vblank, write all 32 shadow colors to $3F00, then perform the palette-address reset sequence.
; Copy the eight-byte descriptor at queueDescriptorPtr into a 32-slot ring. Carry set means full; carry clear means accepted. One slot remains unused to distinguish full from empty.
; Select producer index times eight and copy the descriptor; advance producer modulo 32.

; NMI consumes all pending eight-byte descriptors. Fields are PPU address low/high, byte count, reserved byte, RAM pointer low/high, stride mode, direction. Direction zero writes RAM to PPU; nonzero reads PPU into RAM with a dummy buffered read. Restore software stride after draining.
; Load count and RAM pointer, select PPU increment 1 or 32 without enabling NMI, then execute the requested transfer.
; Write count bytes from transferPtr to PPUDATA; count zero wraps to 256 bytes.
; Discard the first buffered PPU read, then copy count bytes into transferPtr.
; Reset PPU address to $2000 and advance consumer modulo 32 before checking for another descriptor.
; Clear the dirty flag and write all 64 attribute shadow bytes, eight at a time, using increment 1. NMI later restores PPUCTRL and scroll.
; Coordinate helpers index little-endian PPU row-address pairs here. The exported interval also preserves its adjacent lookup bytes; row inputs are caller-controlled, not checked here.
; A selects one of four 8 KiB CHR banks. Read and write the same ROM latch-table byte twice so CNROM bus conflicts preserve the intended low bank bits; PRG mapping does not change.
; Four bytes $30..$33: one literal for each CNROM CHR bank, read and written at the same ROM address to tolerate bus conflicts.
; Return carry clear when musicActive is nonzero, set when zero, by subtracting it from zero.

; A selects one of six supported music pointers (0..5); incoming carry selects looping. Stop current playback, load four instrument selectors ($FF skips), save the sequence restart pointer and initialize the first pattern.
; Read a pattern index and transposition byte from the song sequence. Resolve a relative pointer from the $D168 table, read its initial tick delay and advance both stream pointers.
; X is channel 0..3, A instrument index. Save its doubled table index and write pulse/triangle/noise control registers as applicable; preserve caller X/Y.
; Clear music and effect activity, zero tonal timer registers and silence noise. The song pointers remain available.
; Set playback active without reinitializing its pointers or tick counters.
; Run music and effect sequencing once per NMI.
; If active, decrement the event delay. A due event decodes packed channel/note records; otherwise reduce active note lengths and silence expired voices.
; Y selects a music channel. Leave it alone while an effect owns that channel; otherwise count down its length, silence on expiry and clear its active-mask bit.

; Read note/channel, duration and next-delay triples before testing duration. The final ignored delay shares the next body initial delay, or the first $FF suffix byte for pattern 5. Zero duration ends a pattern and advances or loops the song. Zero next-delay batches simultaneous notes; pending-mask bits determine which hardware voices to update.
; The high two note bits select channel, low six bits plus transposition select pitch. Save doubled pitch index and duration, and mark the channel active and pending.
; Send only newly staged voices to hardware, skipping any channel currently reserved by a sound effect.
; A selects voice and Y indexes pitch words. Pulse and triangle use timer tables; noise uses the fixed noise setup. An active effect takes priority over music on its voice.

; A selects an effect pointer. Request termination of an existing effect and wait a frame before replacement. Header selects voice and initial register bytes; subsequent stream records are timed pitches or control changes.
; Count down effect delay; $FF or a negative activity flag terminates and restores music instrument state. $FE changes control bytes; other values select a pitch with a following duration byte.
; Silence the effect voice, restore the saved music instrument control bytes and clear effect activity.
; Interpret $FE as a three-byte control command; otherwise write a pitch-table pair and take the next byte as delay.
; Data; Static; physical 2571..2905
; Packed audio tables: voice masks, pitch timer words and instrument register pairs; consumers retain the established layouts.
; MusicPointers: Six absolute little-endian sequence pointers, indexed by supported song selectors 0..5. First target is the byte after the table. StartMusic supplies fixed PRG context [0,1,2,3].

; MusicSequence0: Four instrument selectors ($FF skips a voice), then pattern 0, its transposition byte and $FF sequence terminator. StartMusic consumes instruments; LoadMusicPattern advances by two; DecodeMusicEvents tests the terminator. Six supported songs each contain one pattern pair.

; MusicSequence1: Four instrument selectors ($FF skips a voice), then pattern 1, its transposition byte and $FF sequence terminator. StartMusic consumes instruments; LoadMusicPattern advances by two; DecodeMusicEvents tests the terminator. Six supported songs each contain one pattern pair.

; MusicSequence2: Four instrument selectors ($FF skips a voice), then pattern 2, its transposition byte and $FF sequence terminator. StartMusic consumes instruments; LoadMusicPattern advances by two; DecodeMusicEvents tests the terminator. Six supported songs each contain one pattern pair.

; MusicSequence3: Four instrument selectors ($FF skips a voice), then pattern 3, its transposition byte and $FF sequence terminator. StartMusic consumes instruments; LoadMusicPattern advances by two; DecodeMusicEvents tests the terminator. Six supported songs each contain one pattern pair.

; MusicSequence4: Four instrument selectors ($FF skips a voice), then pattern 4, its transposition byte and $FF sequence terminator. StartMusic consumes instruments; LoadMusicPattern advances by two; DecodeMusicEvents tests the terminator. Six supported songs each contain one pattern pair.

; MusicSequence5: Four instrument selectors ($FF skips a voice), then pattern 5, its transposition byte and $FF sequence terminator. StartMusic consumes instruments; LoadMusicPattern advances by two; DecodeMusicEvents tests the terminator. Six supported songs each contain one pattern pair.
; Remaining packed effect pointers and audio records; unchanged consumer contracts apply.

; spriteDefinitionPtr starts with rows and columns, followed by tile/attribute pairs. X/Y supply pixel origin. Skip tile zero; write nonzero tiles into OAM backwards from spriteSlot, moving eight pixels per column/row. This does not update spriteSlot.
; Traverse the same rows/columns and tile-zero holes as DrawMetasprite, setting used OAM Y positions to $F0.

; Convert the A/Y two-byte value by repeated division by ten. Stack remainders to emit most significant digit first into decimalTiles at offset X, storing digits plus one and a two-byte zero terminator. Return X after the last digit.

; Divide the two-byte dividend in mathLo/mathHi by divisor over eight shift/subtract steps. Return quotient in mathQuotient and remainder in mathHi; callers supply a nonzero divisor and a quotient that fits in a byte.

; Initialize display, show legal screen and title, then initialize each battle, deploy fleets and alternate player/computer turns. A loss repeats the battle; victory advances battle/rank. Absolute battle 40 enters ending and credits before a new campaign.
; Clear rank, battle and special-code flags before entering the title menu.
; Check the terminal battle index, initialize rank-dependent fleets and inventories, then run placement and computer deployment.
; Set active side to player and execute a turn. If enemy fleet survives, switch to computer; otherwise process victory.
; Play victory music, increment absolute battle and display the next password; advance five battles per rank and eight ranks per campaign.
; Play ending music, run ship/fireworks scene and credits, then restart at campaign initialization.

; Resolve rank setup list. Clear both six-ship active arrays and eleven-weapon inventories, then enable listed entries. Initialize remaining hull cells from the six-entry size table, reset statistics and AI queue, and hide sprites.
; Add A to the player's 16-bit shot count, propagating carry.
; Add A to the player's hit count.
; Add A to the computer's 16-bit shot count, propagating carry.
; Add A to the computer's hit count.
; Prepare result screen and palettes. Convert the next battle's packed decimal password into display characters, show victory/terminal text, and wait for a changed Start input.
; Show defeat text and statistics. Start exits; Select temporarily shows the computer board, then redraws this screen.
; Blank, hide sprites, select CHR bank 1, decode result background, read attributes and draw rank/battle plus both sides' statistics.
; If a direction nibble is present, use its horizontal/vertical lookup deltas to adjust gridX/gridY, then clamp the footprint within 12 by 8. Carry reports whether a direction was processed.
; Four signed coordinate deltas indexed by each two-bit direction group; neutral and opposed-direction combinations follow the literal table.
; Clamp signed top-left coordinates to zero and ensure footprint width/height stay inside the 12-column, 8-row board.
; Return A times twelve using shifts and addition; A must be a board row.
; Return 12*Y+X using scratch bytes; no bounds checking is performed.
; Save A as cellIndex, repeatedly subtract twelve, return column X and row Y without updating the grid cursor.
; Compute cellIndex=12*gridY+gridX.
; Convert index A to X/Y and store both grid cursor coordinates.
; A is doubled ship type plus orientation. Load footprint dimensions, invalidate cached preview coordinates and show the ship's descriptive text.
; If the coordinate along the cached strip is unchanged, reuse its saved background; otherwise restore the previous strip and capture the new one. Overlay the footprint and queue its new pixels.

; Save packed cursor position. Capture four PPU rows (horizontal) or columns (vertical) into previewOriginal via queued reads, waiting between batches, then copy the 96-byte backing buffer for overlay work.
; Use PPU increment 32, sixteen-byte columns and four captures for a vertical preview.
; Copy the 96-byte unmodified strip to previewComposite before drawing the moving ship.
; Queue the original preview strip back to the board.
; Queue the composed preview strip back to the board.
; Use cached PPU coordinates and orientation to issue four row/column writes; source pointer advances by 24 horizontal bytes or 16 vertical bytes between strips.
; Write four vertical strips using PPU increment 32 and successive screen columns.
; Resolve the oriented ship tile rectangle. Its first two bytes are rows/columns; copy tiles into previewComposite at twice the cursor coordinate with stride 24 horizontal or 16 vertical.
; Twelve little-endian pointers for six ship types in two orientations. OverlayShipPreview reads row/column headers followed by tile rectangles.
; Toggle orientation only if swapped dimensions fit at the current origin. Reject with an error effect; otherwise restore old strip, select new dimensions and recapture/redraw the preview.
; Check footprint bounds, then scan every cell through boardPtr. Carry clear means all zero; carry set means overlap or off-board. Preserve footprint height across the row scan.
; Fill the footprint through boardPtr with the oriented ship's identity byte from the table; preserve footprint height and leave cellIndex at its origin.
; Twelve identity bytes for oriented ships. StampShipFootprint repeats one value over the selected footprint; low nibble identifies the ship.

; A is ship identity, X message index. For computer-side display temporarily build attack scene; show sinking text and run explosions. Mark matching board low nibbles with $40, then restore the appropriate board/status view.
; Six text pointers selected by sinking message index. Text uses the normal zero-terminated renderer.
; Initialize three staggered explosion channels and a four-frame ship sequence. Tick channels for four 50-frame windows, then allow 50 frames for remaining explosions to finish.
; Three-channel launch delays, base pixel positions and OAM allocation bases used by RunSinkingExplosions; indexed as parallel byte arrays.

; A negative frame starts a channel with random small offsets and a sound. Count down its frame delay; hide the old metasprite, advance through five frame definitions and redraw at base plus offsets, or mark inactive.
; Five frame-definition words followed by five frame delays; TickExplosionChannel stops after frame index 4.
; Hide the old sinking metasprite and advance through four definitions; stop drawing after the last frame.
; Four metasprite definition words consumed by AdvanceSinkingShipFrame; no draw occurs once the index reaches four.
; A chooses one of five cell graphics descriptors (pointer and palette bits). Convert board coordinates into two-by-two nametable coordinates and dispatch the rectangular tile/attribute writer.
; Five four-byte records: tile-rectangle pointer, attribute palette bits, and a preserved extra byte. DrawBoardCellState uses the first three fields.

; A selects nametable; X/Y tile origin, sourcePtr rectangle with row/column header. Queue each row at PPU stride 1. Merge palette bits into the relevant two-bit attribute quadrant using its mask, then mark attributes dirty.
; Derive attribute index from groups of four tiles and quadrant from each coordinate's bit 1. Shift palette bits by two per quadrant and mask the previous bits away.
; Four masks preserve the other three two-bit attribute quadrants while replacing the selected quadrant.
; nmiPaletteMode indexes three handler words, resolved through nmiDispatchPtr. Mode zero returns, the other modes animate palette groups.
; Three little-endian code pointers: no effect, board palette cycle, attack palette cycle. The NMI mode must remain 0..2.
; No NMI palette animation selected.
; Every eight frames copy eight colors from one of eight records to background palette slots 4..11, upload and wrap the phase modulo eight.
; Eight eight-byte color records for background slots 4..11, one record every eight NMI frames.
; Every eight frames copy four colors from one of three records into background palette slots 0..3, upload and wrap modulo three.
; Three four-byte background color records, advanced every eight NMI frames.
; Resolve one of twelve oriented-ship text pointers and tail-call the text writer at fixed row 22/column 4.
; Twelve words point to ship-name text for the oriented-ship selector.
; Render the fixed blank text strip at row 22/column 4.
; Zero-terminated blank strip used to erase the ship-name row; kept as original character bytes.
; Use default column 15/row 22 for the player's statistics panel.
; Copy player shots/hits into panel scratch and draw three rows at X/Y: shots, hits and computed percentage.
; Use the default statistics origin for the computer panel.
; Copy computer shots/hits into panel scratch and draw the same three-row panel at X/Y.
; Map the label through the font table, convert the 16-bit shot count to decimal tiles with leading blanks, queue the resulting row and wait a frame.
; Format the byte hit count with leading blanks and queue the row below the shot count.

; Compute hits*100 divided by shots using shift/add and the byte divisor helper, then draw the decimal result and percent sign two rows below the panel origin. Zero low shot count yields zero; this is the original byte-oriented calculation.
; A selects nametable, X/Y origin, sourcePtr a zero-terminated text string. Select stride 1 and enter the common text-to-tile staging path.
; Same text writer, but use PPU stride 32; its historical wide-mode name refers to this alternate stride, not a doubled glyph width.
; Subtract ASCII space and translate through FontTileMap into previewOriginal. Queue the staged byte count using the selected stride, then wait a frame so shared scratch may be reused.
; 64-byte character-to-tile lookup, indexed by text byte minus ASCII space. Renderer assumes its strings stay inside this alphabet.

; Prepare board and battle banner, scroll it into view with music, then place each enabled ship. Ask whether to accept; rejection clears placement and repeats. Return with display blank and music stopped.
; Clear all 96 board cells and reset the placement-record length.

; Set boardPtr to playerBoard. Iterate six enabled ship types, initialize horizontal orientation and cursor, respond to directions/A/B, and save accepted placement records. Invalid overlap/bounds plays an error effect.
; Wait for each frame; directions repeat after a short delay, changed A validates/stamps and changed B rotates.
; Append oriented ship type and origin cell index to the two-byte placement list; increase its byte length.
; Draw ACCEPT SETUP text and a two-choice sprite cursor. Select/left/right toggles with a repeat delay; a changed A/B confirms. Return the selection in carry through LSR, then hide the cursor.
; Select board CHR/palettes/background for the active side, replay saved ship placements and overlay miss/hit graphics across 96 cells. Enable board palette cycling and reveal display.
; Display the player board until a changed Start, then blank and stop palette animation.
; Scan 96 enemy cells and render known miss/hit/sunk states from their high nibbles; unknown cells remain background.
; Preserve cursor, scan enemy cells marked $40, change their state to $80 and render the final sunk tile with a brief delay per cell.
; Prepare the enemy-knowledge background, player statistics and selected weapon. Restore saved targeting cursor, draw its footprint and reveal display.

; Start with weapon zero and origin cursor. Directions move the weapon footprint; Start views own board (and optional enemy-board code), Select cycles available weapons, A/B executes selected attack and waits before returning.
; Handle one targeting frame, including direction repeat timing and changed high-nibble buttons.

; For most weapons build the attack animation scene. Resolve the selected handler, scan the footprint mask and execute nonzero cells, preserving origin. Consume nonbasic ammunition unless the infinite-ammo code is active; stop animation and blank afterward.
; Resolve one of eleven weapon handler pointers, save origin, and scan width by height mask bytes. Each nonzero mask cell calls the indirect trampoline; mask index tracks per-cell sprite slots.
; Eleven code pointers, one per weapon. ExecutePlayerWeapon dispatches once per nonzero footprint mask cell.
; Most weapon cells redraw the attack ship before jumping through weaponHandlerPtr; weapon 4/6 skip that setup. Handler returns directly to the caller of this trampoline.

; Increment shots and inspect the enemy cell. Empty cells become misses; occupied unprocessed cells increment hits, reduce that ship's remaining cells and decrement fleet size on sinking. Repeated hits do not reduce hull twice. Animate result and wait.
; Show scan tiles for this footprint slot; a previously unknown cell with ship identity 1 flashes the positive result. This reveals a scan animation without mutating board state.
; Nine OAM offsets indexed by footprint mask index, used for the type-one scan flash.
; As above, but any nonzero ship identity triggers the positive scan animation; processed cells show the ordinary result.
; Four OAM offsets for the smaller any-ship scan footprint.
; Preserve Y, choose one of eight impact positions, fly an approach sprite toward it, then draw/hide four timed splash frames with sound.
; Two parallel eight-byte impact coordinate tables, selected by three random bits for distant splash animation.
; Preserve Y, choose one of eight impact positions, fly an approach sprite toward it, then draw/hide the corresponding four explosion frames with sound.
; Two parallel eight-byte impact coordinate tables for distant explosion animation.
; Choose one of four direction/definition records. Initialize pixel origin relative to impact, move by signed deltas once per frame until both coordinates reach impact, then hide the projectile.
; Four metasprite words, starting X/Y offsets and signed X/Y increments for the four approach directions.

; Clear computer board and placement list. For each enabled ship choose random orientation and origin, reject overlap/adjacency and repeated alignment with a small random exception. After 255 random attempts scan for a free footprint; restart fleet if none fits. Stamp and record each accepted ship.
; Bound random attempts by the wrapping counter; accepted candidates must pass footprint collision and surrounding-cell tests.
; Scan board origins deterministically for a collision-free footprint; if impossible restart the whole computer deployment.
; Clear 96 enemy board cells and reset its placement-list length.
; Clamp a one-cell border around the candidate rectangle and scan it for occupied enemy cells. Carry set rejects adjacency; clear allows it.
; Append orientation/type and origin to the enemy placement list as a two-byte record.
; Rejection-sample a four-bit random value for X<12 and another for Y<8, producing a uniformly bounded board origin.
; Prepare a diagnostic/reveal board, replay enemy ship placements and overlay its miss/hit cells. Enable board palette cycling and reveal the result.
; Show the enemy board until a changed Start input; blank and stop palette animation afterward.

; Draw own target view and choose weapon geometry. Prefer queued scan discoveries, then hit-pattern inference, then special-weapon scoring; otherwise animate a random walk until a valid target is selected. Execute its footprint, wait, blank and disable palette animation.
; Pop the eight-slot scan target queue when nonempty. Otherwise try pattern-based targeting and special-weapon planning, falling back to a random-search cursor.
; Choose a random origin and move cursor for 24 delayed random steps, then reject processed or unsuitable cells according to rank and minimum remaining hull size.
; Animate one-cell horizontal steps, then vertical steps, until the cursor matches aiTargetX/Y; redraw footprint and wait eight frames between steps.
; Choose independent -1/0/+1 deltas for both axes and clamp X to 0..11, Y to 0..7.
; Hide ordinary cursor sprites, resolve the computer handler and scan active weapon-mask cells. Consume nonbasic ammunition unless the special code is active, then restore cursor origin.
; Eleven code pointers for per-cell computer weapon behavior; same mask traversal contract as player handlers.
; Tail-jump through weaponHandlerPtr; its target RTS returns to the footprint loop.
; Update computer shot/hit statistics and the player board. Reduce remaining hull and active fleet only on the first hit, animate sinking as needed, and preserve cursor around that scene.
; Scan a footprint slot for previously unprocessed ship identity 1. A positive scan appends X/Y to the eight-slot AI target ring and flashes the result; the ring has no separate full check.
; Nine OAM offsets used by the computer type-one scan handler.
; Scan for any previously unprocessed occupied cell, queue positive X/Y targets and animate the scan result.
; Four OAM offsets used by the computer any-ship scan handler.
; Preserve Y, animate a falling projectile at the board cell, then timed splash frames and the persistent miss tile.
; Preserve Y, animate the projectile then explosion frames and the persistent hit tile.

; Compute impact pixel coordinates from grid cell, start the projectile at Y=$F0, and advance two pixels per frame through wrap until reaching the target. Leave its metasprite visible for the caller to hide.

; Search 2x2 squares with three hits and one unknown, then horizontal/vertical hit runs and separated-hit patterns. Return carry set with aiTargetX/Y when a candidate is found; clear means no supported pattern.
; On row Y, find adjacent hits and look forward then backward along their run for an unknown cell. Return its column in aiTargetX with carry set.
; On column X, find adjacent hits and search down then up for an unknown cell. Return row in aiTargetY with carry set.
; Scan a row for a hit, probe hit distances 2..4, and try an unprocessed gap or neighboring unknown. Preserve the original candidate coordinate when a direction fails.
; Vertical companion to the separated-hit search; scan a column, test distance 2..4 and choose an unknown gap cell.

; Probe left/right/up/down at distance A from aiTargetX/Y. Only board state $20 counts as a hit. Return direction 3/4/1/2 and carry set on success; preserve X/Y. Clear carry if no bounded probe matches.

; Starting at a random direction, try up to four bounded neighbors and check whether unknown/hit runs can accommodate the smallest remaining ship. Failure discards the return address into FindHitPatternTarget, then returns carry clear directly to ComputerTurn. This intentional stack unwind abandons the remaining pattern searches.
; Check bounded left, right, up and down cells around aiTargetX/Y using the unknown-cell predicate. Carry set if any is unprocessed; no board mutation.

; Consider scarce special weapons based on surviving fleets, ship associations, remaining hull cells and rank-weighted random thresholds. For a chosen weapon build geometry and score all legal origins; carry reports whether a target was found.

; For every origin where the footprint fits, sum the high-nibble states of cells covered by the mask. Keep all minimum-score origins and rejection-sample one at random. Return its X/Y through aiTargetX/Y and carry set; no candidates clears carry.
; At the candidate origin scan mask width/height and accumulate player board high nibbles into aiOriginScore. Nonzero mask cells contribute; board contents are not changed.
; Use A as a player ship index; compare its active flag to 1 and return the comparison flags.
; Check nonzero computer ammunition and, when the weapon has a ship association, that the corresponding computer ship remains active. Carry reports usability.

; From X/Y scan left over unknown/hit cells, then count the compatible horizontal run; compare its length against minimumShipWidth. The rightward loop tests after incrementing: it can read logical column 12 once, aliasing the next row (or computerBoard on the bottom row). Preserve this original edge behavior; carry is the length comparison.

; Vertical companion: scan upward then count compatible cells downward, comparing to minimumShipHeight. The downward loop can test logical row 8 once before its limit check, reading the adjacent computerBoard storage. This is the original arithmetic, not an extra board row.
; Load aiTargetX/Y and enter the unknown-cell predicate.
; Convert X/Y to index and return carry set only when the player cell high nibble is zero. Ship identity in the low nibble does not affect this test.
; Load aiTargetX/Y and enter the unknown-or-hit predicate.

; Return carry set for player board high nibble zero or $20; other processed states clear carry. Direct target callers use bounded X/Y; the run-measurement helpers can also pass the one-past-edge coordinate described at their entries.
; Start minimum dimensions at 1. Scan six active player ships and use the first surviving type's horizontal width and vertical height table entries as AI fit limits.
; Draw the selected weapon's icon and two descriptive strings. During the player side also display remaining/initial hull cells for its associated ship, when one exists.
; Three arrays of eleven words: icon definitions and two descriptive text rows, indexed by doubled weapon index.

; Wrap through eleven entries, skipping empty ammunition and weapons whose associated ship is sunk. If no alternative exists play the error effect; otherwise initialize the selected geometry and status.

; Resolve the selected weapon record: width, height, base cursor tile, followed by width*height mask bytes. Set footprint dimensions and mask pointer, hide sprites, reset grid origin, and update cursor/status according to active side.
; Traverse mask cells; hide four OAM sprites for each nonzero cell while advancing the OAM offset only for present cells.
; Clamp footprint, convert origin to pixel coordinates and traverse mask. Draw a two-by-two sprite square for each nonzero cell, stepping sixteen pixels across/down.
; Write four consecutive tiles, shared palette attribute 2 and two-by-two pixel positions to OAM at cursorOamOffset. Advance that offset by sixteen bytes.
; At cursorOamOffset replace four consecutive tile numbers; preserve sprite positions/attributes for scan flashing.
; Clamp weapon origin to board bounds and compute pixel X=32+16*gridX, Y=31+16*gridY for drawing.

; Select title CHR/palettes/background, scroll title into view and start music. Draw START/CODE sprite text and selector; directions/Select toggle, A/B/Start accepts. CODE enters the four-digit editor. Port-2 Select cycles music tracks as a built-in title feature.
; Advance random seed each frame and handle music test, menu selection and activation. Accepted password exits to campaign; invalid/special codes keep the menu active.
; Initialize four decimal digits and selected column. Up/down wrap digit 0..9, left/right select bounded column, with twelve-frame repeat delay. Changed Start packs and validates the code.

; Pack digit pairs into two BCD bytes and compare 43 password words. Ordinary indices set absolute battle and rank/battle lookups; indices 41/42 enable persistent special flags and request staying at menu. Index 40 is the ending code: these two lookup reads run one byte beyond the 40-entry rank/battle tables into the next adjacent object, but CampaignMain tests absolute battle first and bypasses battle setup. Carry clear accepts, set rejects or handles a special code.
; Draw four digit sprites at fixed origin; blink the selected digit's palette using frame bit 5. OAM base comes from cursorOamOffset.
; Hide the four password digit sprites starting at cursorOamOffset.
; Place one arrow sprite at the START or CODE row according to menuChoice.
; Render zero-terminated text from sourcePtr as consecutive eight-pixel sprites. Subtract ASCII space for tile numbers, use attribute zero and advance cursorOamOffset.
; Draw the fixed title metasprite using the last OAM slot as its backwards allocation base.

; Blank, choose CHR bank zero and palettes, clear nametable/attributes, load legal-screen attributes and draw text lines. Reveal, require an initial delay, then wait up to another 120 frames or changed Start; blank on return.

; PasswordWords: 43 little-endian packed-decimal words. Indices 0..39 select campaign battles, 40 selects ending, 41 enables infinite ammunition and 42 enables enemy-board reveal. ValidatePassword searches all 86 bytes.

; PasswordRankIndices: Rank index for each ordinary battle 0..39, five entries per rank. Ending code index 40 reads the adjacent first battle-index byte; that value is bypassed by the terminal absolute-battle test.
; PasswordBattleIndices: Battle-within-rank index for ordinary battle 0..39. Ending code index 40 reads the adjacent ASCII digit zero; it is bypassed before setup.
; PasswordDigitCharacters: Sixteen printable hexadecimal characters plus zero terminator; victory password rendering selects decimal nibbles from this alphabet.
; WeaponShipAssociations: Eleven ship associations. $FF means no supporting ship; other entries index the six active/hull arrays for selection and status display.

; ShipHullSizes: Six initial hull-cell counts: 1,2,3,4,5,8, indexed by unoriented ship type.
; ShipWidths: Twelve footprint widths for six types times two orientations; the orientation bit is the low index bit.
; ShipHeights: Twelve corresponding footprint heights. AI minimum-height selection uses the vertical orientation entry at base+1.
